summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with malaise, productive cough with yellowish-green sputum, shortness of breath, and left ear pain. Initial chest X-ray showed no acute infiltrates, but CT chest revealed bronchial thickening and centrilobular nodules consistent with active infection. He was started on IV Vancomycin and Zosyn for suspected pneumonia, later transitioned to oral levofloxacin. ENT confirmed otitis media, treated with otic drops. His acute kidney injury, likely prerenal from volume depletion, resolved with IV fluids. Coumadin was restarted for atrial fibrillation. He improved clinically, remained afebrile, and was discharged home on oral antibiotics, with plans to initiate Revlimid for multiple myeloma and follow up with ENT and anticoagulation clinic.
